relations.myth: Krishna blows cow-dust from Radhika’s face
relations.note: Krishna’s intimate gesture marks Radhika as his favored cowherd beloved.

relations.myth: Krishna publicly favors Radhika over the other cowherd women
relations.note: Krishna’s attention to Radha diminishes the other gopīs’ honor.

relations.myth: Separation, rebuke, submission, reconciliation, and union
relations.note: Radha rejects the unfaithful Krishna before their reconciliation and sexual union.

relations.myth: The single divine reality appears as the eternal pair
relations.note: Radha and Krishna are conjoint Brahman, one essence appearing as two.

relations.myth: Radha embodies Krishna’s intrinsic bliss potency
relations.note: Gauḍīya theology identifies Radha as Krishna’s complete hlādinī-śakti.

relations.myth: Radha emerges from Krishna’s left side in Goloka
relations.note: Radha emanates from Krishna’s left side as his primordial feminine power.

relations.myth: Brahmā secretly marries the pair at Bhāṇḍīravana
relations.note: Radha becomes Krishna’s lawful consort through a secret forest marriage.

relations.myth: Brahmā officiates Radha and Krishna’s secret marriage
relations.note: Brahmā solemnizes the divine couple’s marriage in the forest.

relations.myth: Radha and Śrīdāman quarrel over Krishna and Virajā
relations.note: Śrīdāman defends Krishna during Radha’s jealous confrontation.

relations.myth: Radha curses Śrīdāman to be born as a demon
relations.note: Radha’s curse causes Śrīdāman’s demonic earthly birth.

relations.myth: Śrīdāman curses Radha to earthly birth and separation
relations.note: His counter-curse condemns Radha to earthly life and prolonged separation.

relations.myth: Radha’s jealous approach sends Virajā into river form
relations.note: Virajā becomes a river when Radha approaches Krishna’s secluded meeting.

relations.myth: Lakṣmī sighs while celestial women praise Radha
relations.note: The poem elevates Radha above Lakṣmī through their contrasting reception.
Later theological systems describe Lakṣmī as Radha’s expansion.
Some systems present Durgā as Radha’s external power or expansion.
One later theological classification treats Durgā as Radha’s sister.
Some Śākta-Vaiṣṇava texts identify Durgā as a form of Radha.
Sarasvatī is represented as a manifestation of primordial Prakṛti headed by Radha.
Sāvitrī is represented as a manifestation of primordial Prakṛti headed by Radha.

relations.myth: Tulasī’s fragrance perfumes Radha’s feet
relations.note: Tulasī attends Radha and serves the divine couple’s sacred groves.

relations.myth: Lalitā organizes Radha and Krishna’s secret meetings
relations.note: Radha’s principal sakhī mediates, defends her, and arranges meetings.

relations.myth: Viśākhā carries messages between the divine lovers
relations.note: Viśākhā serves Radha as a principal companion and messenger.

relations.myth: Krishna’s attention to Candravālī provokes Radha’s anger
relations.note: Candravālī rivals Radha and embodies a contrasting mode of divine love.

relations.myth: Campakalatā coordinates Radha’s adornment and secret meetings
relations.note: She assists Radha with dress, messages, reconciliation, and rendezvous.

relations.myth: Citrā coordinates Radha’s adornment and secret meetings
relations.note: She assists Radha with dress, messages, reconciliation, and rendezvous.

relations.myth: Tuṅgavidyā coordinates music and the lovers’ meetings
relations.note: She assists Radha through music, messages, reconciliation, and rendezvous.

relations.myth: Indulekhā coordinates Radha’s messages and secret meetings
relations.note: She assists Radha with dress, messages, reconciliation, and rendezvous.

relations.myth: Raṅgadevī coordinates Radha’s adornment and secret meetings
relations.note: She assists Radha with dress, messages, reconciliation, and rendezvous.

relations.myth: Yogamāyā arranges the lovers’ Vraja meetings
relations.note: She orchestrates circumstances enabling Radha and Krishna’s intimate līlā.

relations.myth: Nārada seeks and praises Radha-Krishna
relations.note: Nārada encounters the pair and disseminates devotion to them.

relations.myth: Shiva discusses and receives Radha-Krishna mysteries
relations.note: Tantric dialogues reveal the couple’s mysteries to Shiva.

relations.myth: Shiva guards or seeks entry to the rāsa
relations.note: Vraja tradition makes Shiva a guardian or aspirant to Radha-Krishna’s dance.

relations.myth: Parvati discusses and receives Radha-Krishna mysteries
relations.note: Late Tantric dialogues involve Parvati in teachings about the divine pair.

relations.myth: Krishna assumes Radha’s emotion and complexion as Caitanya
relations.note: Caitanya embodies Krishna experiencing Radha’s love and golden complexion.
Later traditions equate Radha with Krishna’s Tamil cowherd beloved Nappiṉṉai.

relations.myth: Radha challenges Krishna after Ariṣṭāsura’s death
relations.note: The demon’s death prompts Radha’s demand that Krishna purify himself.

relations.myth: Sacred rivers fill Radha’s newly excavated pond
relations.note: The personified holy waters fill Rādhā-kuṇḍa after her companions excavate it.
